blind_spot: The drill-intent marker is a POSITIONAL THIRD ARGUMENT, and a positional argument is exactly the kind of thing a wrapper drops in silence. Concretely checkable in one step: any tab that later writes `onDrill={(next) => onDrill(next)}` instead of passing the prop through degrades m09 back to today's behaviour — a bucket row would navigate to the customer card instead of drilling — and NOTHING goes red, because the shell tests call ReportSurface directly and the tab tests mock onDrill. Today all four tabs pass onDrill through unwrapped and say so in writing (tabs/executive/surfaceKit.jsx: 'נמסרים לשלד כפי שהתקבלו, בלי עטיפה'), which is why I chose the argument over a field in the object — a field would have to be deleted before every URL write, and one forgotten delete sends the server a p_drill key it does not know. Both designs trade one silent failure for another; I picked the one whose precondition is greppable (`grep -n onDrill src/modules/11_reports/tabs/`). The durable fix is for onDrill to take one object ({ drill, row, intent }) so nothing is positional — a contract change across four tab owners, which is why I did not make it in a fixer round.
